authorisation: D74 (2026-10-26), continued under the same mission and PR #251 (the Product Owner's final-acceptance finding: the routing fingerprint is exposed by reads and derived only from current state; and a controlled rollback must not silently weaken Shared STRICT). It does NOT authorise merging PR #251 (the head-specific approval was not applied by the agent), Go-Live, or any live network, routing, PMS or financial action by the agent.
gap_found: The apply compared a fingerprint of the current routing, which ordinary reads returned. It proved the state had not moved, not that this exact change had been previewed and accepted by this operator, and a change away and back restored the same fingerprint, so an approval older than both changes would have been accepted again.
changes: A preview that can be applied mints a server-held, single-use, 15-minute proposal bound to the network, the previewing operator, the exact mode and interfaces, the network's change counter and its routing. Reads never expose it. The apply and the removal are refused unless every binding holds (other operator, other content, any change to the network since, expired or used); any applied change retires all of that network's proposals.

Removal is previewed (mode UNDECIDED) and confirmed with DELETE ?proposal=; the previous policy and interfaces are audited. pms_routing.previewed, pms_routing.policy_set, pms_routing.cleared and pms_routing.proposal_refused carry the proposal id and reason.

scripts/binary-rollback.sh refuses to install an scd or edged that predates the room sign-in policy while any Shared STRICT policy exists (artifact marker plus live count; unreadable is a refusal; no override). 0155.down.sql refuses while a shared policy exists. Both leave everything unchanged and name the operator action.
The Admin Console confirms with the proposal of its own preview, returns to step 1 when the proposal can no longer be confirmed, and previews the removal before it can be confirmed.

verification: Before: Go unit and integration tests on a fresh full-schema PostgreSQL (edged including the real svc_edged role, scd, pmsresolve), 47 binary-rollback cases, 1028 console unit tests, lint, typecheck and 27 browser tests for the changed areas. Regression tests: reads expose nothing that authorises a change; an invented, empty, old-style or fingerprint request changes nothing; a proposal confirmed for other interfaces, another policy or as the other kind of change is refused; a proposal works once; an approval made before two changes that restored the same state is refused; an obsolete removal approval removes nothing; the removal preview lists and audits what it removes; the store binds operator, network and content, expires, and is bounded; the down migration refuses with a shared set and runs without one; the rollback tool refuses scd and edged targets without the policy while shared sets exist, refuses an unreadable or non-numeric count, and allows a policy-aware target or zero shared networks. On a disposable database as iam_v2_owner: the down migration was refused with 26 shared networks (nothing changed), ran after they were converted, saved 68 policies, and the re-apply restored them. After deployment: reads carry no authorising value; seven invalid or old-style requests against a non-existent network were refused; a valid preview returned its own proposal and was not applied; invalid previews minted none; every network's policy and interfaces identical before and after; the rollback tool, in --dry-run against a real pre-policy edged build, read the live database (0 shared networks at that moment) and replaced nothing. NOT verified: the refusal path of the rollback tool against a live shared network (none exists on PRE-LIVE: the Product Owner's networks are dedicated); a real client signing in; real Protel behaviour with two interfaces on one network; tagged-VLAN delivery on the switch/ESXi side.
product_owner_live_testing_observation: PRE-LIVE kept changing under the Product Owner's own admin account after the previous receipt (audit): further recovery, Access-to-Trunk changes (one rolled back), a second PMS interface created, routing set for Client Wi-Fi and a new network, backups and guest-data operations. These were their actions; the agent performed none. Two previews I made on the Default Network (valid, never applied) are in the audit as pms_routing.previewed.
